neighbours.label: vertical air motion in weather: rising or sinking air, thermals and Foehn winds
fire: Over the hot desert the warm air rises quickly and forms tall clouds by evening.
As the descending air sinks down the lee slope it warms and dries out.
Glider pilots circle inside thermals to climb without an engine.
A warm, dry Foehn wind blew down into the valley and melted the snow.
Strong updrafts lift moist air high into the storm, where it freezes.
Subsiding air under the high-pressure ridge keeps the skies clear for days.
In the afternoon, convection carries the heated air upward over the mountains.
The chinook roared down from the Rockies and raised the temperature twenty degrees.
quiet: Over the hot desert the air stays dry and the sky is clear by evening.
On the lee slope the meadow is dry and the grass turns brown.
Glider pilots check their maps carefully before every flight.
A cold rain fell over the valley and the snow turned to slush.
Strong storms brought heavy rain to the coast, where roads flooded.
Under the clear skies the farmers harvested the wheat for days.
In the afternoon, the hikers carried their packs over the mountains.
The storm came in from the west and lowered the temperature twenty degrees.

notes: Card: Foehn (x3), sinking air, warmer air rises, CAPE; logit effect suppresses temperature, atmosphere, rising. Label at the meaning level (vertical air motion).
